title: Assigned to me shows only columns with my work orders and hides pinning
custom_preconds:
1. Sign in to the build under test as a user whose role has Work Orders view and Work Orders create and edit (check in Settings > Roles & Permissions > open your role > Work Orders section). The Admin role has both.
  2. Use a desktop browser with the window at least 1024 pixels wide (full screen on an ordinary laptop or monitor). Below that width the page shows only List.
  3. In the top bar, choose the location you will test in (e.g. "Heavy Duty"). Create everything below in this location.
  4. Make sure the location has the technicians this case uses (e.g. "Esther Howard", "Ralph Edwards", "Jenny Wilson" and yourself (Clockable on, enrolled here)). A person only counts as a technician here when the staff record is Active, Clockable is on, the role is neither Office nor Time Clock User, and they are enrolled at this location. To add one:
    • Settings > Staff > add a staff member > enter the first and last name (e.g. Esther Howard), role Technician, Clockable on, Active, enrolled at this location > Save.
  5. Create the work orders this case uses and set their lead technician (e.g. S1-702 led by you, S1-691 led by Ralph Edwards, S1-352 with no lead, nothing for Jenny Wilson):
    • Work Orders > New Work Order > choose a customer (e.g. "Fibridge Commercial") and an asset (e.g. unit TRK-118, 2022 Freightliner M2) > Create. Write down the number the build gives the work order (the numbers in this case are examples).
    • On the work order page set Lead Technician (e.g. Esther Howard) and save. Leave Lead Technician empty on the ones that should sit in Unassigned.
  6. On S1-352 set the Service Advisor to yourself so an unassigned work order is "assigned to me" (if List with Assigned to me on does not show it, assign yourself as technician on one of its lines instead).
  7. Pin Jenny Wilson in Board View before you start.
custom_steps:
1. Open Work Orders.
  2. Click the All tab on the left of the toolbar.
  3. In the display switcher at the right of the toolbar, click Board View (in the design its tooltip reads "Board").
  4. Turn on Assigned to me.
  5. Read every column shown.
  6. Look at the column headers for a pin control.
  7. Turn Assigned to me off.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • With Assigned to me on, Board View shows only the Unassigned column (holding S1-352) and your own column (holding S1-702).
  • Ralph Edwards, Esther Howard and the pinned Jenny Wilson are hidden.
  • No column header offers a pin control while Assigned to me is on.
  • Turning Assigned to me off brings back every column and the pin controls, with Jenny Wilson still pinned.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-10043; story SV-10046 (Story 3, Board View — board by lead technician); PRD Confluence 845185030, edited 7 Oct 2026 (status line "PRD v33"), S3-N1, S3-N3, read 8 Oct 2026. Review Decisions 853901313 DR-42.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S3-N1: “With Assigned to me enabled, Board View shows only the technician columns, including Unassigned, that hold at least one work order matching Assigned to me (S1-R13). Every other column is hidden, including pinned technicians.”
  • S3-N3: “Do not offer pinning while Assigned to me is enabled.”
